title: Battle of the Boyne
description:
The **Battle of the Boyne** was fought on July 1, 1690 (July 12 in the modern calendar), between the forces of the deposed King James II and those of King William III near the town of Drogheda on the east coast of Ireland.

William's forces, composed of Dutch, English, Scottish, French Huguenot, and Danish troops, defeated James's army of Irish Catholics and French troops. The battle was a key moment in the Williamite War in Ireland.

The battle has remained a significant symbolic event in Irish history, particularly for Protestant communities in Northern Ireland, who commemorate it annually on July 12. It remains a politically sensitive topic due to its association with sectarian divisions.
